newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF revises up Australia barley forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF revises up Australia barley forecast.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) said on Monday it had revised upward its 1996/97 barley production forecast to 6.15 million tonnes from 6.03 tonnes in its previous estimate.

While the Queensland state barley harvest has finished, some late barley still has to be harvested in northern New South Wales, the private forecaster said. The late harvested grain is showing signs of weather damage from two rain storms, although most barley harvested early, including crops in the north were of malting quality, the AWF said.

Queensland should produce 460,000 tonnes of barley in 1996/97, well up on the 211,00 produced in in 1995/96, the AWF said. Exceptions were two western areas, which received late frosts, resulting in small-grained barley, it said.

Later-harvested barley in southern New South Wales and north eastern Victoria states is making malting classification, the AWF said. Samples are pale in colour, but the colour is not uniform, following a late November rain, it said.
While it proved a good year for South Australia, yields were not quite up to last year, AWF noted.
Production in 1996/97 should total 1.90 million tonnes, unchanged from the previous forecast, versus 2.02 million in 1995/96.
"Quality in the core malting barley production areas of Yorke Peninsula, the Mid North and the South Australian mallee is excellent," AWF said.
Western Australia's barley prospects improved with two October rains, it said.
"The barley sown in in the Great Southern areas germinated late, but in the event had ample growing time to produce satisfactory yields and good quality," AWF said.
However, samples from the southern areas are not as bright as the trade expects from the region, AWF added.

Western Australia's barley output is forecast to reach 1.30 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 1.20 million in the previous estimate, AWF figures show. The latest Australia-wide forecast exceeds the 1995/96 figure of 5,962 tonnes.
Australia's barley year commences April 1 and ends March 31.
